name: Question 18
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4y & =5 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}-4y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=8$ and $y=11,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)-8\cdot 4 & =0 \\ 2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-32 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $x,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $y=11$ into the equation of the parabola.  

At the point where $y=11,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4y & =5 \\ {x}^{2}-4(11) & =5 \\ {x}^{2}-44 & =5 \\ {x}^{2} & =49 \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $x>0$ since we're only interested in the first quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $x=7,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-32 & =0 \\ 2(7)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-32 & =0 \\ 14\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =32 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{32}{14} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{16}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
